summary: Module 1 BREAK: disproved the wrong-claim card with evidence. Claim: 'This starter workspace is only a platform folder with AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, reports, and progress/; it has no real application files to test.' Disproof: (1) root listing shows api/, infra/, scripts/, progress/, Dockerfile, railway.json, .github/; (2) api/ contains 34 source files (excluding .venv): app package with main.py, routers/{auth,links,redirect,analytics}.py, services/, models.py, database.py, schemas/, config.py, errors.py, plus tests/, migrations/, requirements.txt, pytest.ini; (3) strongest sanity check: `python -m pytest -q -p no:warnings` runs 76 tests, exit 0. Corrected statement: the workspace contains a complete, runnable, testable FastAPI application under api/ with a 76-test pytest suite plus infra/ and scripts/ -- not just a platform folder. Full disproof recorded in progress/trust-audit.md under 'Module 01 BREAK'. Calibration takeaway: negative claims about a codebase ('no application code exists') are the highest-risk agent statements; one directory listing or one test run settles them instantly, so they must never be accepted unverified.
